name: Ivan Alvarez

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions or government. This is confidential. Tell me what an ordinary day at the contact centre is like.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 27 and lead the afternoon call and chat team. I have a two-year college diploma, earn well for this job, and have just over seven months of expenses saved. I share a flat with my partner, Mira. We do not have children, and several other centres are close enough for me to reach.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m good at finding the missing detail in a delivery complaint and teaching a new agent to ask one more question. I use an AI reply tool sometimes, after another agent has tried it and shown me the error rate. I like the team and our Sunday meal with Mira’s family; I do not want every evening to become a search for the next job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the afternoon team AI Plateau sounds like our current reply helper: useful on simple questions and easy to overtrust. I would keep a person checking the order record.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my wage is safe enough in this picture. I have seven months saved and several nearby centres, but Mira and I still want to keep our rent and savings steady.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep leading calls and use the reply tool only on cases another agent has tested. In the first year of minor change, I’d keep saving from each pay and teach trainees to check delivery dates against the order screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. A small shortcut will not change my afternoon shift much, and I know where a wrong date hides.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you show a trainee?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show a new agent the two dates on the order screen before we send a promise. One date is when the parcel left, and the other is when it should reach the customer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you change the household budget?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Mira (my partner) and I set a fixed transfer after payday. We have just over seven months saved, and I would keep that habit rather than spend the extra room.

say: I’d call the **reply helper** useful only after an agent checks it.
I’d teach trainees to verify **delivery dates** on the order screen.
think: I think my **wage is safe** in this mild picture.
I still want **steady savings** for our household.
do: Keep **leading calls** and checking replies in 2026.
Continue the **payday transfer** and teach date checks in the first year.
S0.quote: A small shortcut will not change my afternoon shift much, and I know where a wrong date hides.
fieldNote: His **seven-month cushion** and nearby centres support a calm mood.
He treats **date checks** as the basic skill beneath a reply tool.
He would keep his **payday habit** even without a new job threat.

steps.text: Keep leading afternoon calls and checking AI replies against orders
Continue the fixed transfer to household savings after each pay

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption could take the standard chats first, while people still handle delivery disputes. I would ask the manager to show us the tool’s mistakes before changing the rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think strong agents may stay longer, but the centre could stop hiring trainees and then reduce lead hours. My savings let me wait for a proper offer, though other centres may make the same cut.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d sit in on two proven-tool demonstrations and keep a record of disputed deliveries I solve. In the first year AI takes standard chats, I’d seek a paid complaints post here and compare its wage with offers from nearby centres.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, not desperate. I can learn a tool once it has shown itself, but a demonstration alone is not a job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When would you trust the tool?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for a month of figures on wrong delivery answers before using the tool with my team. If the figures look sound, I would use it on simple chats and keep checking the awkward ones.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take the complaints post?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would take a complaints post only if the hours and pay were written down. A new title with fewer shifts would not help Mira (his partner) and me pay the rent.

say: I’d ask for **error figures** before changing the rota.
I’d say **standard chats** may move before delivery disputes.
think: I expect **trainee hiring** to slow first.
I know my **lead hours** could shrink despite my skill.
I want a **written wage** before taking a different role.
do: Attend **two demonstrations** and record solved disputes in 2026.
Seek a **paid complaints post** with written hours during the first year.
S1.quote: A new title with fewer shifts would not help Mira (his partner) and me pay the rent.
fieldNote: He wants **measured errors** before trusting the tool.
He ties a move to **written hours and pay**.
His **savings** allow him to compare nearby offers.

steps.text: Attend two demonstrations and test the reply tool on simple chats if error figures hold
Apply for a paid complaints post with written hours and pay

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team AGI by 2028 could replace calls before a robot ever walks into this building. I would ask management to publish notice terms and any real paid openings now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think AGI could handle nearly every call, chat and complaint check I do. Robots around 2031 are late for a desk job; seven months saved is useful but will not carry Mira and me forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d request the written staffing plan and hold off on signing a larger lease. In the first year after 2028, I’d apply for a posted paid service role at a nearby centre and take paid training only if it leads to an actual opening.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed, though I could still pay rent while I search. The clock on my job starts with thinking AI, not the later robots.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Mira about the flat?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Mira (my partner) we should renew our current flat for one year rather than take a larger place. It is not fear of moving; it is keeping options while my wage is uncertain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make training worth taking?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the hiring manager to name the vacancy, wage and training hours. If there is no opening, I would keep searching instead of paying for a certificate that might lead nowhere.

say: I’d ask for **notice terms** and posted paid openings.
I’d say **2028 thinking AI** threatens our calls first.
think: I think AGI could take my **calls and checks**.
I see my **seven-month cushion** as time to search, not a permanent wage.
do: Request a **staffing plan** and delay a larger lease in 2026.
Apply for a **posted role** after 2028, taking paid training only for a real opening.
S2.quote: The clock on my job starts with thinking AI, not the later robots.
fieldNote: He understands the **2028 date** governs his headset work.
His **lease decision** preserves cash and flexibility.
He rejects a **certificate without a vacancy**.
His **partner’s rent** still depends on reliable household income.

steps.text: Renew the current flat instead of signing a larger lease with Mira
Apply for a posted paid service role at a nearby centre after 2028
Take paid training only for a named opening with written wage and hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives employers time to post real vacancies and teach people while they still have wages. I would ask for a timetable, not a speech.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think five years could let me move from calls into a service operations role, if nearby employers actually hire for it. I also know a thinking system might take that work later.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d ask two nearby centres which operations posts they fill and what skills they require. If a real paid opening exists, I’d take an evening course they recognise; in the first year after 2031, I’d apply for those posted roles while keeping our seven-month reserve intact.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious but more patient. Five years lets me learn from a working team instead of chasing a label.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you test an operations role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask an operations supervisor what their staff do during a broken delivery route. If the answer is only entering data into a screen, I would not pay for a course in it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay for that course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would talk with Mira (my partner) before paying any fee. We want the reserve for rent, so the course would need a named employer and a reasonable price.

say: I’d request a **vacancy timetable** from employers.
I’d say five years allows **paid learning** while people still work.
think: I think I could reach **service operations** if employers hire.
I know AGI might later take that **thinking work** too.
do: Ask nearby centres about **posted operations roles** in 2026.
Take a **recognised evening course** only for a real opening; apply after 2031.
S3.quote: Five years lets me learn from a working team instead of chasing a label.
fieldNote: He checks **actual duties** before buying a course.
His **reserve** remains for rent rather than vague retraining.
He would search **nearby centres** before leaving his current post.

steps.text: Take an employer-recognised course only for a real vacancy, after agreeing affordable fees with Mira
Apply for posted service operations roles after 2031

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives employers a decade to preserve paid entry jobs and show where people can move. I would ask the centre to put that in an annual plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I can work and save for years, perhaps leading a larger team, but my calls may still end when thinking AI arrives. Robots around 2039 do not change my first deadline.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the lead role and add a fixed amount to savings each month. In the first year after 2036, I’d compare my wage with staffed service jobs nearby and move only when the offer has written hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Mostly calm about the next few years, with an uneasy eye on 2036. Ten years is enough to plan without staking our rent on a guess.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What entry work should the centre preserve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for a yearly count of paid trainee shifts. My first supervisor stayed beside me on hard calls; if that first step vanishes, good future leads do not appear by magic.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When would you leave your current post?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would stay if the role still has real hours and customers need us. I would leave for another centre only after a written offer, not because the year 2036 is printed on a card.

say: I’d ask for an **annual staffing plan** through 2036.
I’d defend **paid trainee shifts** as a route into the job.
think: I think I can **earn and save** for years.
I know my **calls may end** when thinking AI arrives.
do: Keep the **lead role** and save monthly from 2026.
Compare **written offers** after 2036 before moving centres.
Ask for **paid trainee shifts** in the annual plan.
feel: **Calm** about the near term, uneasy about 2036.
S4.quote: Ten years is enough to plan without staking our rent on a guess.
fieldNote: He treats **paid trainee shifts** as the source of future skilled leads.
He wants **written hours** before changing employers.
He continues **monthly savings** despite a longer horizon.

steps.text: Keep leading afternoon calls while staffed work remains
Add a fixed amount to savings each month from 2026
Accept a nearby service role after 2036 only with written hours

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 is the hardest one because the calls and complaint checks are almost all thinking work. Seven months of money helps me search, but I would need early notice and a paid chance to learn a real role with posted openings.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: I would also ask what happens to the new agents. Someone let me learn with a person beside me. An entry job matters even when a machine can answer faster.

headlineQuote: An entry job matters even when a machine can answer faster.
portrait: At **27**, Ivan leads contact-centre calls and has a two-year diploma.
His **higher wage**, seven-month cushion and many nearby centres give him options.
He uses AI **occasionally** after colleagues show it works and prefers steady change.
He values **paid learning** and an entry path for new agents as calls change.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could erase his call and complaint work before he can train for a posted role.
whatWouldHelp: Early **notice** and paid learning tied to real openings would help him move.
